skill.description: Create Codex-compatible custom pet spritesheets from a public reference image using RunComfy, GPT Image 2, and ImageMagick assembly steps.
skill.summary: Generates a Codex Pet spritesheet and manifest from one reference image with RunComfy and ImageMagick.
skill.author: runcomfy-com

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown formatting false positives, not executable Ruby backticks or hidden behavior. The skill intentionally asks users to run RunComfy and ImageMagick commands, sends a source image URL to a third-party service, and writes assets into the Codex pets directory. The main actionable issue is unvalidated PET_NAME usage in local paths.

remediation.issue: Pet names are used directly in run and install paths.
remediation.suggestion: Accept only simple pet names such as lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores. Reject slashes, dot segments, and shell metacharacters.

remediation.issue: Source image URLs are processed by a third-party service.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit user consent before remote generation. Warn users not to provide private images, signed URLs, or confidential project assets.

remediation.issue: pet.json is written with shell-expanded values.
remediation.suggestion: Generate the manifest with a JSON writer or escaping step so quotes and newlines cannot corrupt the file.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The shell recipe builds directories directly from PET_NAME and then runs mkdir and cp. The default value is safe, but the instructions do not constrain user-supplied names.

content.user_title: Create Codex Pet Sprites with RunComfy
content.value_statement: Custom Codex Pet sprites require a precise atlas and manifest. This skill turns one reference image into a RunComfy-generated pet package for Codex.
actual_capabilities: Generates a canonical pet image through the RunComfy GPT Image 2 edit endpoint.
Normalizes the generated image into transparent 192x208 Codex Pet cells.
Assembles a 1536x1872 spritesheet with nine required animation rows.
Creates a pet.json manifest for Codex custom pet loading.
Installs output into the Codex pets directory when the shell steps are approved.
Documents frame counts, tuning options, and RunComfy troubleshooting codes.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account token, and ImageMagick.
Sends the source image URL to RunComfy for remote image processing.
Uses one generated pose, so animation is subtle and transform-based.
Pet names should be sanitized before using the install path.

use_cases.title: Create a Personal Coding Companion
use_cases.description: Turn a public mascot or avatar image into a custom Codex Pet package.

use_cases.title: Prepare Contest Submissions
use_cases.description: Generate Codex-compatible pet assets with the required atlas size and animation rows.

use_cases.title: Batch Pet Concepts
use_cases.description: Use repeated runs to compare multiple source images with consistent output structure.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Basic Pet
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Codex Pet from this public image URL: [URL]. Use the default name my-pet and explain each generated file.

prompt_templates.title: Generate and Install After Approval
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with a custom name.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Codex Pet named build-buddy from [URL]. Preserve the source identity and install it only after I approve.

prompt_templates.title: Tune the Chroma Key
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request when magenta conflicts with the subject.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate the pet package from [URL]. Change the chroma-key to cyan and keep all atlas dimensions compatible with Codex.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Multiple Pets
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for several public image URLs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Batch create three Codex Pets from these public image URLs. Use sanitized names, separate run directories, and summarize any failed generations.

output_examples.input: A user provides a public mascot image URL and asks for a pet named build-buddy.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a canonical pose, normalized frames, a spritesheet.webp atlas, and a pet.json manifest.

output_examples.input: A designer requests stronger jumping and review motion.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies row changes, adjusts transform values, and keeps the required frame counts for Codex.

output_examples.input: A developer asks to install the finished pet.
output_examples.output: The skill copies the manifest and atlas into the Codex pets folder after confirming the target name and path.

best_practices: Confirm the RunComfy token and external image URL before running remote generation.
Use simple lowercase pet names with hyphens and no path separators.
Keep a separate run directory for each pet to avoid overwriting outputs.
anti_patterns: Run the shell recipe with a private or expiring image URL without consent.
Use unsanitized pet names that contain slashes, dots, or shell metacharacters.
Change atlas dimensions or row frame counts after generation.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a Codex Pet package with spritesheet.webp and pet.json files for local Codex loading.

faq.question: Does it require Codex Pro?
faq.answer: No. It uses a RunComfy token and CLI instead of the Codex imagegen skill.

faq.question: What tools must be installed?
faq.answer: The workflow needs the RunComfy CLI and ImageMagick available on the local machine.

faq.question: Where are files installed?
faq.answer: The install step writes into CODEX_HOME or the default HOME .codex pets directory.

faq.question: Is my source image sent to a third party?
faq.answer: Yes. The source image URL is processed through RunComfy and related model services.

faq.question: Can I customize animation?
faq.answer: Yes. Adjust ImageMagick transform values while keeping the required dimensions and frame counts.
